terra.problem: Calling Ahithophel David's former counselor brings in a fact from outside the passage without a reference.
The final line repeats that Hushai wasn't quiet rather than delivering a joke or adding insight.
Saying Hushai never breaks a sweat adds an unmarked claim about how he handles the encounter.
The text says Absalom and all the elders liked the proposal, not that everybody in the room did.
The text does not say everybody in the room nodded, or even who else was in the room.
It invents a reason for Hushai's wording: that he is being careful because of the respect for Ahithophel's advice.
The text compares Ahithophel's advice to consultation of the word of God, not to the word of God itself.
The text does not say Hushai is guessing about David's location.
It asserts that Hushai wants Absalom worried, a motive the text does not give.
It asserts that Hushai wants Absalom to feel fear, a motive the text does not give.
Saying the word is meant to scare assigns Hushai an unstated intention.
Calling Ahithophel David's former counselor brings in a fact from outside the passage without a reference.
Hushai says David is surely hiding in a cave or some other location. The explanation changes that to probably hiding in a cave.
The explanation is flat and repetitive: it rules out a storeroom, quotes the well, then twice restates where they hid.
The text gives no basis for saying a stable would have been much easier to search.
The text does not say the covered well looked like ordinary work.
The text does not say the servants went in the direction the woman described, or that her statement caused the search to fail.
The text does not say the servants searched the place the woman named or that her statement kept them busy.
The text says the servants did not find the men, but does not say nobody checked under the grain.
By daybreak does not mean the crossing took until morning light. The text also does not say they crossed one person at a time.
The text does not say how long the crossing took, so calling it fast work adds an unsupported detail.
The text says Ahithophel went home, but does not establish that he was never riding toward David along the way.
